claims.finding: PVH's Calvin Klein women's dress and suit licences expire on 2026-12-31 after twenty years, returning that revenue in-house at PVH's own margin - a dated structural step-up in FY2027 revenue and gross margin that the pre-print coverage in this capture flags as overlooked, published two weeks before the print under the headline 'the deadline Wall Street forgot', against a stock at roughly 6.5x forward earnings with a 10.5% short float.

claims.why_not_priced: Two houses downgraded this stock in the ten weeks before the print - BofA to Underperform with a $70 target on 2026-06-25 and JP Morgan to Underweight on 2026-08-04 - and neither, as relayed here, engages with a licence reversion that mechanically lifts owned-brand revenue and margin from the first day of 2027. The corpus contains no news document that discusses it either; the only place it appears in 151 captured items is one independent research relay. The stock meanwhile fell 16.97% over twenty sessions to $72.29, which is where the JP Morgan downgrade's own raised $84 target sits well above the price - an incoherence the corpus itself remarks on. The print is the natural forum for management to size the reversion into FY27, and a 10.5% short float is the fuel if they do. The band's low end is only -1 because this is a January-2027 economic event: it cannot make this quarter's numbers, so its worst case is simply that it goes unmentioned.
